title: The Screenshot Test: What Teens Should Check Before Sending an Angry Message
summary: A quick parent-and-teen check for turning one angry draft into a clearer choice before it leaves the phone.
seo_title: Angry Teen Message: The Screenshot Test
seo_description: Before your teen sends an angry message, use the ten-step SCREENSHOT check to review the facts, audience, tone, safety risks and the best next move together.
release_move: Keep adult ownership of danger and account safety while returning ordinary send, edit, pause, channel and repair choices to the teenager.

core_belief_shift.from: I need to take the phone or ban angry texting to stop my teenager making the conflict worse.
core_belief_shift.to: I can hold the safety line, coach one quick pre-send check, and let my teenager increasingly own ordinary communication choices and repair.

book_relevance.reason: The War Playbook is a restrained optional bridge for teens who want practice reading pressure, checking facts and weighing the cost of reacting; this guide stands alone.

hero.alt: A concerned mother waits in a bedroom doorway while her teenage daughter types an angry message on her phone.

social_image.alt: A concerned mother gives her teenage daughter space while the teen types an angry phone message.

next_step.reason: Optional teen practice for reading pressure, checking facts and choosing which conflicts are worth entering.
